name: Yusuf Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say publicly and what you actually think. What is a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Yusuf, 58, and lead developers at a tech company that runs departure screens for small rail stations. I have a master’s degree and can usually find why a platform change reached the control desk but not the public sign. I trace the event log, phone the station supervisor and review a fix with the team. I use AI now and then for test ideas, but I read the real train movement record myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does the job fit the household?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Amira cooks paid meals for local events, and our children are grown. My lead pay is low for the work and her bookings come in unevenly. We have a mortgage, around two weeks of expenses saved and few similar developer jobs nearby. Retirement is in sight, but we have not verified what would pay our bills if we stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the station AI Plateau still leaves someone needing to make a platform change visible before passengers move. A correct control log cannot put a traveller on the right train.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I worry about a quiet month of Amira’s event bookings and our two-week reserve. My lead job is secure, but the mortgage does not pause for a cancelled meal order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking event logs against station supervisors’ reports and sign off on public display fixes. I’d set aside 25 on paydays only after mortgage and groceries are covered. In the first year I’d use AI only with invented train times, not private travel or operator records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about ordinary cash, even if AI changes little. Knowing the sign system well does not make the bill account bigger.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which missed update affected passengers?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A platform changed after a late train and the desk knew, but the hall screen stayed on the old platform. I found the missed update before the next service.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Amira buy another oven?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amira and I would keep the kitchen oven running instead of buying a larger one. We need paying orders before more equipment.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave people checking public platform signs.
I would compare **station reports** with event logs.
think: I worry **event catering** can have quiet months that leave mortgage cash short.
Our **two-week reserve** barely protects mortgage payments when event orders are cancelled.
do: **Check** station reports against logs and sign off display fixes.
**Use** AI only with invented train times, and keep the old oven rather than buy a larger one.
feel: **Anxious** about thin savings despite steady lead work.
S0.quote: A correct control log cannot put a traveller on the right train.
fieldNote: His **lead expertise** connects station calls to display logs, using AI only for invented cases.
The **two-week buffer** and variable catering bookings create baseline mortgage worry.

steps.text: Keep checking platform displays against station reports with lead sign-off
Save 25 only after mortgage and groceries
Keep current oven rather than buy a larger one before paid catering orders

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption can write and check sign code and answer passengers before robots handle platforms. I would keep a station supervisor able to stop a wrong automatic platform message.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think our firm may leave my lead role while cutting colleagues, then ask me to cover more stations for the same hours. Amira’s bookings may also be sensitive to customers cutting event spending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my manager for paid time to learn AI testing of platform changes using twelve old cases with travel details removed. I’d try it only if a station supervisor reviews every proposed message and management approves the privacy rules. In the first year, if my paid hours fall, we would stop the music subscription and apply only to real software posts with a written wage that, with Amira’s usual booked meals, covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my own hours later and Amira’s orders now. I will use a proven test, not turn passengers into a live experiment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which platform change tests the new method?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One train changed platform twice in ten minutes. I would use that case because a tidy one-change test misses what passengers actually see.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Amira add orders?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amira would count accepted paid meal orders, not conversations about next season. An inquiry about my wife’s catering is not money we can spend.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to reach sign code before platform robots.
I would retain **supervisor control** over automatic platform messages.
think: I expect **colleague cuts** could widen my workload.
I worry **catering orders** could dip as event budgets change.
do: **Learn** AI platform testing only on approved paid time, twelve de-identified cases and supervisor review.
**Keep** private travel details out under management-approved rules.
**Cancel** music subscription and seek real posts if paid hours fall, only when signed wages plus Amira’s booked meals cover mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about later own hours and current catering uncertainty.
S1.quote: An inquiry about my wife’s catering is not money we can spend.
fieldNote: His **AI learning** needs paid approval, privacy rules, twelve old cases and supervisor review.
A **job search** starts only if paid hours fall and a real wage covers bills with booked catering.

steps.text: Learn AI platform tests only with paid approval, twelve de-identified cases and supervisor review
Cancel music subscription if developer hours fall
If hours fall, apply to real posts whose written wage plus booked catering covers mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches display-code thinking work in 2028, with hands-on platform robots around 2031. Amira’s menu planning might change before a robot cooks meals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect even my lead post could go. Two weeks saved will run out before a long search, and the few local software firms may not be hiring either.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for written layoff terms and contact the mortgage lender before missing a bill if dismissed. We would cancel our planned summer family visit before paying fares and hold cash for food and housing. In the first year after 2028, if my post ends, I’d apply to real paid openings and eligible income help, without treating grown children’s wages or unbooked catering as ours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed and unable to sleep well over the mortgage. Two years will not turn my lower lead pay into a retirement fund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would children pay for the visit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children we must postpone the visit. I would not put the train fares on a card and hope they repay us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would catering protect you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amira would keep cooking for customers who have actually booked and paid. A full calendar of inquiries is not cash.

say: I expect **2028 AGI** to reach sign code before 2031 platform robots.
I would say **menu planning** changes before hands-on cooking.
think: I expect my **lead post** could go.
I cannot count on **local software hiring** after full thinking AI.
do: **Request** written layoff terms and contact lender early if dismissed.
**Cancel** summer family visit before fares and hold mortgage cash.
**Apply** to real paid openings and eligible help if post ends after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing pay with a two-week buffer.
S2.quote: A full calendar of inquiries is not cash.
fieldNote: He expects **2028 code loss** before hands-on platform robots around 2031.
His **thin cash buffer** leads to early lender contact and postponed travel, without assumed family income.

steps.text: Cancel summer family visit before buying train fares
Apply to real paid openings if dismissed after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if dismissed after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 reaches display code in 2031 and platform robots around 2034. Five years lets me test whether small stations will pay for an on-site sign and evacuation-message rehearsal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect software pay to be at risk. I know the display system, but an unpaid favour for a station manager is not a second income after full thinking AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d seek written employer clearance and ask two station operators for paid weekend rehearsal orders, using their own screens and no passenger data. I’d accept only if contracts cover travel, insurance and my time, and Amira agrees the weekends do not crowd out her paid events or our family time. In the first year after 2031, if coding ends, I’d continue only with repeat paid orders and human demand despite 2034 robots; otherwise I’d seek actual paid openings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the code wage, with a small test I can price before doing it. I will not buy display equipment for a station that has not signed an order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the rehearsal check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A rehearsal should ask a passenger where the exit message sends them when the usual stairs are shut. I would need the station operator there to approve the wording.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who decides which weekend is free?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amira and I would put her accepted catering jobs on the calendar first. The rehearsal fee must justify travel and leave us some shared time.

say: I expect **2031 AGI** to reach code before 2034 platform robots.
I would test **paid station rehearsals** through actual orders.
think: I expect **display-code pay** could shrink when full thinking AI reaches rail systems.
I cannot treat **unpaid station favours** as a second wage for our mortgage.
do: **Seek** written employer clearance and two paid station orders using station screens, no passenger data and operator-approved wording.
**Accept** only contracts covering travel, insurance, time and Amira’s event and family calendar.
**Continue** after 2031 coding loss only with repeat human paid demand; seek real posts otherwise.
feel: **Anxious** about code pay, with a priced limited trial.
S3.quote: I will not buy display equipment for a station that has not signed an order.
fieldNote: His **weekend rehearsal trial** requires clearance, written orders, station screens and no passenger data.
Continuation needs **repeat net paid demand** and weekends that do not displace Amira’s events.

steps.text: Rehearse only with employer clearance, paid orders, station screens, operator-approved wording and cost-covering fees
Keep Amira’s booked events and agreed family weekends clear of rehearsals
After 2031 coding loss, continue only with repeat paid human demand despite approaching robots
Seek actual paid openings if rehearsal demand fails after coding loss

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell friends AGI by 2036 reaches display code in 2036 and hands-on platform robots around 2039. A decade lets us check paid work and our real retirement figures rather than trusting a calendar age.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I worry the firm could squeeze lead hours before 2036, and catering orders still vary today. Two weeks saved and no verified pension amount give us no reason to promise retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking platform signs with supervisors and save 25 only after mortgage and groceries. Amira and I would request written retirement statements and a mortgage balance each year. In the first year after 2036, if code work ends, I’d seek real paid work; I would retire only if documented income and savings cover housing and ordinary bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the thin buffer despite ten years. Warning time matters only if paid work keeps coming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you set a retirement date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare our own retirement statements with the remaining loan. Our children’s incomes are not part of that calculation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the next developer need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would hand the next developer the record of each double platform change. The passenger sees the public sign, not the neat event log.

say: I expect **2036 AGI** to reach code before 2039 platform robots.
I would check **written retirement resources** against housing bills.
think: I worry **lead hours** could shrink before the full 2036 coding change arrives.
I know **two weeks saved** cannot fund retirement while the mortgage remains unpaid.
do: **Keep** supervisor-checked signs and save 25 only after essentials.
**Request** annual retirement statements and mortgage balances with Amira.
**Seek** real paid work if code ends after 2036; retire only with verified resources.
feel: **Anxious** about baseline thin savings despite a decade.
S4.quote: The passenger sees the public sign, not the neat event log.
fieldNote: He keeps **supervisor-checked work** and small conditional savings while verifying retirement resources against the mortgage.
The **retirement gate** excludes guessed pensions, unbooked catering and grown children’s incomes from household calculations.

steps.text: Keep checking public platform signs with station supervisors while paid
Save 25 only after mortgage and groceries
Seek real paid openings if code ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our two-week buffer would go before another software offer appears. Written terms, a real paid opening, eligible help and early lender contact would matter. I would rather earn the next wage than rely on our children.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the station supervisor where a passenger goes when the platform sign is wrong. The train does not wait for a perfect log.

headlineQuote: The train does not wait for a perfect log.
portrait: Yusuf is a **58-year-old lead developer** with a master’s degree, lower pay and two weeks saved.
He uses **AI occasionally** for invented platform tests, checking real events with station supervisors.
His wife’s **catering orders** vary, leaving their mortgage exposed to ordinary cancellations.
He tests **paid station rehearsals** only with employer clearance, written orders, covered costs and preserved family time.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could empty the two-week buffer before a local software offer appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written terms**, a real paid opening, eligible help and early lender contact would matter.
